title: Man assaulted with hammers in cryptocurrency robbery at home
seoTitle: Man attacked with hammers in crypto robbery
subtitle: Robbers threatened to kill a pregnant woman's baby to force a transfer of hundreds of thousands of pounds.
excerpt: Criminals broke into a home, beat a man with hammers and threatened a pregnant woman's baby to demand a cryptocurrency transfer.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Criminals broke into a residence and attacked a man to steal digital assets. During the crime, the intruders beat the victim with hammers and threatened the baby of his pregnant wife, demanding the delivery of funds held in virtual currencies.

The man endured continuous blows with the tools until he carried out the requested fund transfer. The violence stopped only after hundreds of thousands of pounds in cryptocurrency were sent to the attackers' control.

Custody of assets and physical security

Cryptocurrencies are managed through decentralized networks. Unlike the traditional financial system, where banks and institutions act as intermediaries able to block anomalous movements or contest coerced debits, the transfer of crypto‑assets depends solely on access to users' private keys.

Once a cryptocurrency transaction is confirmed, it becomes final and irreversible. This technical structure means investors who hold direct control of their access codes can become targets of physical coercion, as the immediate surrender of passwords gives unrestricted control of the funds to third parties.

Protection mechanisms for digital currencies

To reduce direct exposure to violent home invasions, there are general custody and wealth‑protection practices aimed at those who hold substantial amounts:

  • Multi‑signature wallets: systems that require approval from more than one private key to release transfers, preventing a single threatened individual from completing immediate transactions.
  • Cold storage: keeping access credentials on offline devices stored away from the residential environment.
  • Discretion about wealth holdings: avoiding public disclosure of large amounts to not attract criminal attention.

The violent robbery highlights the risks faced by virtual‑asset holders when armed individuals use physical coercion to obtain direct, irrevocable access to digital wallets.

With information from BBC News.
